intro: Every chapter of the book grew out of particular conversations. This guide points to the moments each chapter draws on, so you can hear them as they happened.

chapters.title: Introduction: Zero Viewers and the Only Way Is Up
chapters.summary: Who we are, why science can’t answer existential questions, and what this book is.

moments.note: Zero viewers, and the only way is up
Matthew happens to have a whiteboard
Can science answer the big questions?

chapters.title: The Universe Is Absurd
chapters.summary: The universe doesn’t care, existence is a nonsense story, and science is the wrong tool for the question of what to do about it.

moments.note: Science can’t pick the best pop song
The universe walks down the street naked
Paley’s watch, and a watch with no watchmaker
What do we do with each day?
Matthew: no meaning we’ve yet discovered

chapters.title: What Is Nihilism, Really?
chapters.summary: Nihilism as frustrated idealism rather than apathy, how it differs from atheism, and why it can be freeing.

moments.note: When calling yourself a nihilist was unacceptable
Running for governor, and 240 votes for president
John Marmysz: the nihilist as frustrated idealist
The self is as made up as God
Nihilism opens a space for something to happen

chapters.title: The Laughing Nihilist
chapters.summary: Laugh at the absurd or be the butt of the joke: humour, incongruity, the uses of pessimism, and nihilism as play.

moments.note: Larry David on a desert island
Any sense of normality is provisional
Andy Kaufman, Lenny Bruce and the wind-up merchant
Yannick Jacob: you make your own rules

chapters.title: The Hard Problem of Being Alive
chapters.summary: Consciousness, the self as a projection, the silicon brain, and when human beings became existential creatures.

moments.note: Peter Hankins: consciousness in an afternoon
The easy problem and the hard problem
The hard problem is really about reality
Ten copies, all called Matthew Smith
Heidegger: animals don’t die, they expire

chapters.title: Pain, Happiness, and the Cult of Positivity
chapters.summary: Why over-valuing happiness makes people unhappy, why pain isn’t harm, and why love and grief come together.

moments.note: When feeling bad feels like failure
To wish away the pain is to wish away the love

chapters.title: Death: The Elephant in the Room
chapters.summary: How we have hidden death away, what a hospice taught Louie, waiting, grief, and Ecclesiastes.

moments.note: Fight Club and the origins of soap
The jolliest person in the hospice
A. A. Gill, and what we’ll be remembered for
Do these experiences help the bereaved?
A hand on the cave wall

chapters.title: What Are We, Anyway?
chapters.summary: Memes, the narrative self, evolution as a ratchet, language as the spark, and a species that selected itself.

moments.note: A narrative structure of mental molecules
Brains as hardware, memes as software
Matthew refills the water for a rose
Helen Keller and the arrival of language
We all pass the Turing test

chapters.title: So What Do We Do?
chapters.summary: Monday mornings, the right to be lazy, passions put in storage, and being condemned to be free.

moments.note: Paul Lafargue’s The Right to Be Lazy
Nobody asks a tree why it isn’t surfing
The freest thing in the universe
You still choose how you do today

chapters.title: The Only Way Is Up
chapters.summary: What we believe, as much as either of us believes anything, and why the conversation is the point.

moments.note: What do we do in a meaningless universe?
Laugh at the absurd, or be the butt of the joke
